summary: Staggered 429 waves caused by short-window refill mismatch during ephemeral-proxy handoff in hybrid embed/chat workload
description:
Issue summary:
Packetwave reports recurring 429 responses in their dedicated pool during a daily high-concurrency job that multiplexes short-lived SSE/websocket embed requests and low-latency chat calls. The 429s arrive in short, regular waves (1–3 minutes) rather than a single sustained throttle; patterns align with ephemeral-proxy handoffs and orchestrator rebalancing.

Impact:
- ~15% of their user-facing chat requests get 429s for brief intervals, causing degraded UX and automatic retry loops in their orchestrator.
- Background embed imports (bulk, short-lived connections) see partial failures that require retrying, increasing cost.

Observed behavior:
- 429s stamped with route=/v1/embeddings and X-Rate-Limit-Reason: window_refill_mismatch.
- Console shows token bucket refill pulses on the edge roughly every 30s but origin refill uses a 60s epoch for the same tenant when ephemeral-proxy IPs change.
- Failures correlate with Packetwave's upload workers that spin up many ephemeral HTTP/2 streams with short TTL keys.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived connections and ephemeral keys should not induce repeated tenant-level 429 waves every refill epoch. Edge and origin should align refill windows or gracefully handle handoff without double-counting.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant with mixed traffic: many short-lived embed upload workers (concurrency 200), plus low-latency chat connections multiplexed via HTTP/2.
2) Rotate ephemeral keys frequently (TTL 45s) and reuse them across workers while keeping connection pooling at the edge.
3) Observe tenant-level token bucket consumption in console; watch for 429 bursts at 30s intervals while origin refill logs show 60s epochs.

comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Raman (customer): We're seeing recurring 429s exactly at 30s intervals during our ingest window. We only get partial success after retries. Can you help us avoid retries and reduce failed requests?

2026-03-10 — Support (Ethan Morales): Thanks, Aisha — we see matching 429 signatures. We're triaging rate-limiter logs and checking alignment between edge refill and origin refill windows. Please share your worker concurrency and ephemeral key TTLs (you included them above; we'll validate against telemetry).

2026-03-11 — SRE (Maya Singh): Initial hypothesis: edge-level token counting uses a shorter refill epoch when connection pool affinity is high (per-proxy IP window). When ephemeral keys move between proxies the origin's tenant accounting resyncs on a different epoch resulting in transient double-counting. Repro steps created; capturing pcap and sampling proxy affinity.

2026-03-11 — Support (Ethan Morales): Provided temporary mitigation to Packetwave: 1) Reduce worker concurrency to 80–100 during ingest window; 2) Increase ephemeral key TTL to 120s to reduce handoffs; 3) Requesting isolated burst pool for their embedding route while we patch. Packetwave will test and report by EOD.

2026-03-12 — Packetwave (Aisha): After increasing TTL to 120s and lowering concurrency to 90 we observed ~90% reduction in 429 waves during test run. Still want a permanent fix so we don't have to throttle ourselves.
investigation_notes: Edge and origin rate-limiter code paths use separate window_epoch defaults; edge uses 30s for per-proxy affinity accounting, origin uses tenant-level 60s. This mismatch surfaces when ephemeral keys cause rapid proxy handoffs.

Observed duplicate credit deduction when a request is counted at edge (proxy A) and origin then re-evaluates the token consumption under a different epoch boundary after the handoff — net effect looks like faster depletion resulting in a 429 spike.
Recreated locally with k6-based harness that simulates 200 short-lived streams with TTL 45s; reproduces 429 waves matching customer pattern.
Hypothesis: two mitigation paths: align refill epochs (config change) or make origin-idempotent accounting that dedupes short-window double-counts keyed by request-id / ephemeral-token fingerprint.

Performance note: changing origin accounting to dedupe requires careful coordination and a migration plan; aligning epochs at edge to 60s may increase perceived burstiness for other tenants — consider tenant-scoped override for dedicated pools.
resolution: Workaround provided (reduce concurrency, increase ephemeral TTL, requested isolated burst pool). Engineering to schedule change: tenant-scoped refill-alignment flag for dedicated pools. Patch PR opened to add a per-tenant config; follow-up rollout planned after tests.
